title: HCA Healthcare Q3 2026 Earnings Beat Estimates as Revenue Rises to $19.85 Billion
excerpt: Adjusted EPS rose 3.7% to $7.22 on revenue of $19.849 billion as admissions grew 3%; an uninsured payer shift cut pretax income by about $400 million, and 2027 earnings were signaled flat.
body:
• HCA Healthcare's third-quarter adjusted earnings rose 3.7% year over year to $7.22 per share, beating consensus estimates of $6.66 to $6.74, while revenue rose 3.6% to $19.849 billion, ahead of estimates near $19.33 billion.
  • Same-facility equivalent admissions grew 3.0% and emergency room visits climbed 5.1%, but same-facility inpatient surgeries fell 1.4% and outpatient surgeries declined 3.7%.
  • A shift toward uninsured patients, mainly people who lost coverage on health insurance exchanges, cut pretax income by about $400 million; a modest increase in Medicaid supplemental payments and improved cost control helped offset the drag.
  • HCA now expects 2026 results in the upper half of its guidance — earnings of $28.70 to $30.50 per share on revenue of $77.0 billion to $79.5 billion — but signaled 2027 earnings generally consistent with 2026.

HCA Healthcare beat Wall Street expectations for the third quarter on Tuesday, as stronger patient volumes and Medicaid supplemental payments cushioned a sharp rise in uninsured care. The country's largest for-profit hospital operator also said full-year 2026 results should track the upper half of its forecast range, even as federal policy changes reshape who pays for hospital care.

Revenue rose 3.6% to $19.849 billion in the quarter ended September 30, from $19.161 billion a year earlier, according to the company's third-quarter release. Adjusted earnings rose to $7.22 per share from $6.96, ahead of the $6.66 per share analysts expected on LSEG data cited by Reuters and the $6.74 Zacks consensus. Net income attributable to HCA fell 3.9% to $1.579 billion, but diluted earnings per share still rose 4.5% to $7.27 as share repurchases cut the share count. Adjusted EBITDA rose 1.2% to $3.918 billion.

Volumes Rise, Surgeries Soften

Demand for hospital and emergency care held up. Same-facility admissions increased 2.7% and same-facility equivalent admissions rose 3.0%, while same-facility emergency room visits increased 5.1%. Same-facility revenue per equivalent admission rose just 0.6%, reflecting the weaker payer mix.

The soft spot was surgery. Same-facility inpatient surgeries declined 1.4% and outpatient surgeries fell 3.7%, a pattern analysts linked to patients losing insurance and deferring elective procedures. Zacks noted that higher admissions drove the beat, while declining surgeries and elevated operating expenses partly offset the gains.

The $400 Million Uninsured Hit

The quarter's central headwind was coverage loss. HCA said a payer mix shift driven by an increase in uninsured volume, primarily patients who lost coverage on the health insurance exchanges after enhanced premium tax credits expired, reduced income before income taxes by approximately $400 million.

"Despite the challenges brought about by federal policy changes this year, our colleagues have continued to provide high-quality care to patients, and we believe HCA Healthcare is positioned to end the year positively."

— Sam Hazen, HCA Healthcare CEO

Offsetting part of that drag, growth accelerated in insured revenue per equivalent admission excluding Medicaid supplemental payment programs, cost performance improved, and the net benefit from those Medicaid programs increased modestly. Operating cash flow was $4.461 billion, up from $4.416 billion a year earlier.

Cash, Buybacks and the 2027 Outlook

HCA repurchased 7.23 million shares for $2.970 billion in the quarter, leaving $4.240 billion under its authorization, and spent $1.357 billion on capital expenditures. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.78 per share, payable December 29 to shareholders of record on December 15. HCA ended the quarter with $908 million in cash, total debt of $50.493 billion, and 189 hospitals plus about 2,600 ambulatory sites across 19 states and the United Kingdom.

For 2026, management now expects results in the upper half of the ranges set in July: earnings of $28.70 to $30.50 per share on revenue of $77.0 billion to $79.5 billion. The longer view is more cautious. On the earnings call, Hazen said 2027 earnings should be generally consistent with 2026, with volume growth of 2% to 3% offset by $550 million to $650 million less in Medicaid supplemental payment benefits and continued pressure from uninsured patients, according to Reuters. A full 2027 outlook is due in January — and shares fell on the flat signal.
